continuity: Prometheus (2012) screen Deacon extended as an internal project lineage
authorityRule: The final on-screen Deacon in Prometheus controls. Abandoned Ultramorph and early Deacon concepts are exclusion evidence, not positive identity references.

sources.use: Official archival production context and practical-creature provenance.
Neal Scanlan demonstrates the blue-hued, taloned Deacon rod puppet and describes the practical-effects direction.
Defines the negative boundary: Huante states that his Deacon was not the screen-selected design and separates the earlier Gigeresque Ultramorph branch from the final creature.
Supports the bishop-mitre head etymology, gangly foal/giraffe proportions, placenta-like iridescent skin and goblin-shark jaw influence through attributed production quotations.

referenceFinding.screenCanon: One newborn Deacon is shown at the end of Prometheus. Its final screen anatomy is the visual authority.
referenceFinding.projectAdaptation: Deacon Line extrapolates that single film individual into a repeatable gameplay lineage. Population, adult scale and full locomotion cycles are project-authored rather than screen-certified.
referenceFinding.conceptBoundary: Ultramorph, Holloway-transformation and other abandoned preproduction branches must not be substituted for the final screen Deacon.

identityLock.silhouette: Tall, slender, eyeless biped with a narrow organic torso, long gangly clawed limbs and a long cranium terminating in a pronounced rear/upward bishop-mitre point.
identityLock.head: Distinct pointed mitre silhouette; not a broad Big Chap dome, not a pale Ultramorph spearhead and not a Neomorph crown.
identityLock.skin: Midnight/navy blue organic membrane, subtly pearlescent and iridescent, wet placenta-like translucency, with natural muscles and joints rather than black ribbed biomechanical armor.
identityLock.mouth: Goblin-shark-like protrusive jaw action, grounded in the final Deacon design; no Predator mandibles or technological mouth parts.
identityLock.limbs: Long bipedal legs and long clawed arms; no quadrupedal default stance.
identityLock.facing: Strict right-facing profile in every source pose.

redesignProhibitions: No Ultramorph or Engineer-host giant anatomy, pale/albino palette, Giger-biomechanical ribbing or abandoned concept-art silhouette.
No tail and no dorsal tubes.
No Big Chap dome, Neomorph white spiked skull, Queen crest or warrior carapace.
No armor, clothing, harness, weapon, cybernetics, Predator technology, neon markings or visible eyes.
No quadrupedal baseline, wing, extra limb or tentacle.
No film logo, text, UI, watermark, environmental collage or cast shadow.

sourceContract.background: flat magenta key or true alpha
poseRules: Complete head, hands, feet and full body inside each nominal cell with safe margins.
No frame may touch or overlap another frame.
No grid lines, labels, numbers, caption, floor, shadow or scenery.
Preserve the same individual, anatomy, scale, lighting and right-facing direction across all eight cells.

idle.motionLock: Grounded bipedal rest with subtle breathing and weight transfer; feet remain physically supported.

move.motionLock: Eight-pose bipedal walk/run cycle with contact, down, passing and up phases; no quadrupedal crawl and no teleporting stride.

attack.motionLock: Claw strike or protrusive goblin-shark jaw strike with anticipation, contact, follow-through and recovery; never a tail strike.

death.motionLock: Loss of support, progressive collapse and terminal grounded pose; no dissolve, explosion or excessive gore.

scalePolicy.futureRigidLandmark: Use a repeatable cranial chord from the front jaw hinge to the terminal mitre point on at least two readable poses per clip. Bounding-box height and width are posture diagnostics only, never the scale authority.
scalePolicy.groundPolicy: Standing and locomotion poses must share one support line; attack may lower the pelvis without changing anatomical scale; death may collapse below standing height.

identityPass: Blue organic bipedal identity is readable.
No tail or dorsal tubes are visible.
identityReservations: The head sometimes reads as a broad horizontal cowling rather than a consistently sharp bishop-mitre point.
The V56 sheet has four poses per clip, not the eight chronological poses required by V66.
Legacy manifest identityVerified metadata is runtime bookkeeping and does not certify film-exact fidelity.

cellMeasurements.interpretation: Idle and move are internally stable in height, while attack and death bounds change with posture. These bounds cannot certify anatomical scale across clips because no rigid landmark was measured.
